challenges.name: rate-limiter-quiz
challenges.title: Was the login limiter broken?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the login brute-force incident: the access log of a burst at a minute boundary, and a limiter that refreshes its TTL on every request.

questions.explanation: False. The limiter did exactly what a fixed window does. The key was created at 10:00:00.000 with a 60 s TTL and expired at 10:01:00.000; the attempts from 10:01:00.050 created a new key and a new budget of five. A fixed window promises at most N per window, not at most N in any 60 seconds, so up to about 2N requests can pass around a boundary - here 9 guesses in under a second. If that is not acceptable for logins, the fix is a different algorithm (a sliding window, or an extra short window such as 3 per 10 s), not a bug fix in this code. The misconception is to read "5 per minute" as "5 in any minute".

True. EXPIRE on every request moves the expiry 60 s into the future each time. With a request every 20 s the key never reaches its expiry, so the counter only grows: 6, 7, 8... and every request after the fifth gets 429, indefinitely, although the real rate (3 per minute) is under the limit. The window is supposed to start with the first request and end 60 s later, which is why the EXPIRE belongs only to the request that created the key (or to a key found without a TTL). The misconception is that refreshing the TTL keeps the window "accurate"; it turns a fixed window into one that never closes while traffic continues.

challenges.name: fixed-and-sliding-window-limiters
challenges.title: Rate limit logins: fixed and sliding windows
challenges.description:
POST /auth/login on the CodeDev API is limited per key ("ip:<address>" or "user:<id>"). A brute-force burst at a window boundary got 9 password guesses through a "5 per minute" fixed window, so the API team wants two limiters on Redis with one contract: return { allowed, remaining, retryAfter }, with retryAfter in whole seconds (0 when allowed) and remaining 0 when denied. Both throw a RangeError when limit or windowSeconds is not a whole number >= 1.

fixedWindow(redis, key, limit, windowSeconds) uses one counter, "rl:fixed:<key>": count = INCR. If the key has no expiry after the INCR (ttl -1: a new key, or one left without a TTL by a process that crashed between INCR and EXPIRE), EXPIRE it for windowSeconds; never EXPIRE a key that already has a TTL. Allowed when count <= limit, with remaining = limit - count. Denied requests are counted too, and their retryAfter is the TTL of the key.

slidingWindow(redis, clock, key, limit, windowSeconds) estimates a sliding window from two fixed windows aligned to the clock, in integer milliseconds: W = windowSeconds * 1000, index = Math.floor(clock.now / W), elapsed = clock.now - index * W; curr = value of "rl:sliding:<key>:<index>", prev = value of "rl:sliding:<key>:<index - 1>" (missing = 0); weighted = prev * (W - elapsed) + curr * W. Allowed when weighted + W <= limit * W: INCR the current key (EXPIRE it for 2 * windowSeconds when the INCR returns 1) and remaining = Math.floor((limit * W - weighted - W) / W). Denied: write nothing, and retryAfter = Math.ceil(waitMs / 1000) with waitMs = W - Math.floor((limit - curr - 1) * W / prev) - elapsed when curr + 1 <= limit, otherwise waitMs = (W - elapsed) + (W - Math.floor((limit - 1) * W / curr)).

Input (JSON on stdin): { limit, windowSeconds, requests: [{ at, key, limit?, windowSeconds? }], seed?, quiet? }. "at" is the fake clock in milliseconds; a request may override the limit or window; "seed" puts counters without a TTL into the fixed-window Redis first. The runner sends every request to both limiters (each with its own Redis) and prints one line per request, for example "60.100s ip:203.0.113.7 | fixed: allowed, 4 left | sliding: denied, retry in 12s" ("error RangeError" for an invalid config), or with quiet a summary per key, and finally how many keys each Redis still holds two windows after the last request.
hints: For each limiter, what is the one Redis key that answers "how many requests has this caller made in the current window", and when must that key disappear on its own?

Fixed window: ttl() returns -1 for a key without an expiry, which is how you recognise both a brand-new counter and one left behind by a crash. Sliding window: compute index and elapsed from clock.now first; the two keys differ only in the index, and everything else is integer arithmetic on curr, prev, W and limit, so you never need a division before the final Math.floor or Math.ceil.

A worked example with other numbers: limit 4, window 10 s, request at 23.5 s, so W = 10000, index = 2, elapsed = 3500. If rl:sliding:k:1 holds 4 and rl:sliding:k:2 holds 1: weighted = 4 * 6500 + 1 * 10000 = 36000, and 36000 + 10000 > 40000, so it is denied. curr + 1 = 2 <= 4, so waitMs = 10000 - Math.floor(2 * 10000 / 4) - 3500 = 1500, and retryAfter = 2. At 25.0 s, weighted = 4 * 5000 + 10000 = 30000 and 30000 + 10000 <= 40000: allowed with remaining 0.
